paragraphs.text: POETRY CHALLENGE

Write a poem about how courage, determination, and strength have helped you face challenges in your life. 
 Prizes

3 Grand Prizes: Trip to Washington, D. C. for each of three winners, a parent and one other person of the winner’s choice. Trip includes round-trip air tickets, hotel stay for two nights, and tours of the National Air and Space Museum and the office of National Geographic World.
6 First Prizes: The book Sky Pioneer: A Photobiography of Amelia Earhart signed by author Corinne Szabo and pilot Linda Finch.

50 Honorable Mentions: Judges will choose up to 50 honorable mention winners, who will each receive a T-shirt in memory of Earhart’s final flight. 
 Rules
Follow all rules carefully to prevent disqualification.
■Write a poem using 100 words or fewer. Your poem can be any format, any number of lines.
■Write by hand or type on a single sheet of paper. You may use both the front and back of the paper.
■On the same sheet of paper, write or type your name, address, telephone number, and birth date.
■Mail your entry to us by October 31 this year.

Jennifer Mauer has needed more willpower than the typical college student to pursue her goal of earning a nursing degree. That willpower bore fruit when Jennifer graduated from University of Wisconsin﹣Eau Claire and became the first in her large family to earn a bachelor’s degree. Mauer, of Edgar, Wisconsin, grew up on a farm in a family of 10 children. Her dad worked at a job away from the farm, and her mother ran the farm with the kids. After high school, Jennifer attended a local technical college, working to pay her tuition (学费) , because there was no extra money set aside for a college education. After graduation, she worked to help her sisters and brothers pay for their schooling. Jennifer now is married and has three children of her own. She decided to go back to college to advance her career and to be able to better support her family while doing something she loves: nursing. She chose the UW﹣Eau Claire program at Ministry Saint Joseph’s Hospital in Marshfield because she was able to pursue her four﹣year degree close to home. She could drive to class and be home in the evening to help with her kids. Jennifer received great support from her family as she worked to earn her degree: Her husband worked two jobs to cover the bills, and her 68﹣year﹣old mother helped take care of the children at times. Through it all, she remained in good academic standing and graduated with honors. Jennifer sacrificed (牺牲) to achieve her goal, giving up many nights with her kids and missing important events to study. “Some nights my heart was breaking to have to pick between my kids and studying for exams or papers, “ she says. However, her children have learned an important lesson witnessing their mother earn her degree. Jennifer is a first﹣generation graduate and an inspiration to her family﹣and that’s pretty powerful.

In the mid-1990s, Toni Bissell taught English as a volunteer in Uzbekistan. He left after seven months, physically broken and having lost his mind. A few years later, still attracted to the country, he returned to Uzbekistan to write an article about the disappearance of the Aral Sea.

His visit, however, ended up involving a lot more than that. Hence this book, Chasing the Sea: Lost Among the Ghosts of Empire in Central Asia, which talks about a road trip from Tashkent to Karakalpakstan, where millions of lives have been destroyed by the slow drying up of the sea. It is the story of an American travelling to a strange land, and of the people he meets on his way: Rustam, his translator, a lovely 24-year-old who picked up his colorful English in California, Oleg and Natasha, his hosts in Tashkent, and a string of foreign aid workers.

This is a quick look at life in Uzbekistan, made of friendliness and warmth, but also its darker side of society. In Samarkand, Mr Bissell admires the architectural wonders, while on his way to Bukhara he gets a taste of police methods when suspected of drug dealing. In Ferghana, he attends a mountain funeral (葬礼) followed by a strange drinking party. And in Karakalpakstan, he is saddened by the dust storms, diseases and fishing boats stuck miles from the sea.

Mr Bissell skillfully organizes historical insights and cultural references, making his tale a well-rounded picture of Uzbekistan, seen from Western eyes. His judgment and references are decidedly American, as well as his delicate stomach. As the author explains, this is neither a travel nor a history book, or even a piece of reportage. Whatever it is, the result is a fine and vivid description of the purest of Central Asian traditions.

According to a recent study in the Journal of Consumer Research, both the size and consumption habits of our eating companions can influence our food intake. And contrary to existing research that says you should avoid eating with heavier people who order large portions (份) , it’s the beanpoles with big appetites you really need to avoid. To test the effect of social influence on eating habits, the researchers conducted two experiments. In the first, 95 undergraduate women were individually invited into a lab to ostensibly (表面上) participate in a study about movie viewership. Before the film began, each woman was asked to help herself to a snack. An actor hired by the researchers grabbed her food first. In her natural state, the actor weighed 105 pounds. But in half the cases she wore a specially designed fat suit which increased her weight to 180 pounds.

Both the fat and thin versions of the actor took a large amount of food. The participants followed suit, taking more food than they normally would have. However, they took significantly more when the actor was thin.

For the second test, in one case the thin actor took two pieces of candy from the snack bowls. In the other case, she took 30 pieces. The results were similar to the first test: the participants followed suit but took significantly more candy when the thin actor took 30 pieces.

The tests show that the social environment is extremely influential when we’re making decisions. If this fellow participant is going to eat more, so will I. Call it the “I’ll have what she’s having” effect. However, we’ll adjust the influence. If an overweight person is having a large portion, I’ll hold back a bit because I see the results of his eating habits. But if a thin person eats a lot, I’ll follow suit. If he can eat much and keep slim, why can’t I?

paragraphs.text: Some individuals are born with a gift for public speaking. __36__   Do you want to be a good public speaker? Here are some principles you must master.

People want to listen to someone who is interesting, relaxed and comfortable. Too often, when you stand up to give a speech, you focus on the “public” at the expense of the “speaking.” __37__   Focus on the speaking. Talk directly to your audience, be yourself and make a connection.

Even the most successful public speaker will make mistakes. Yet, the only one who cares about any mistake is the one who is speaking. People’s attention wanders constantly. In fact, most people only absorb about 20 percent of a speaker’s message. So, don’t stop speaking when you make a mistake unless it’s a truly serious one. __38__
Your goal is not to be a perfect public speaker. __39__   And like everything else in life, that takes practice. Remember, even world champion athletes practice their skills on a consistent basis.

__40__   It’s rare to hear someone say, “I wish that speaker had spoken longer. “ On the other hand, you probably can’t count the times that you’ve thought, “I’m glad that talk is over. It seemed to go on forever!” So surprise your audience. Always make your presentation just a bit shorter than anticipated. It’s better to leave your listeners wishing for more than shifting restlessly in their seats waiting for your speech finally to end.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, __56__ (wealth) people travelled and collected plants, historical objects and works of art. They kept their collection at home until it got too big __57__until they died, and then it was given to a museum. The 80, 000 objects collected by Sir Hans Sloane, for example, __58__ (form) the core collection of the British Museum __59__opened in 1759.
The parts of a museum open to the public __60__ (call) galleries or rooms. Often, only a small part of a museum’s collection __61__ (be) on display. Most of it is stored away or used for research.

Many museums are lively places and they attract a lot of visitors. As well as looking at exhibits, visitors can play with computer simulations (模拟) and imagine__62__ (they) living at a different time in history or __63__ (walk) through a rainforest. At the Jorvik Centre in York, the city’s Viking settlement is recreated, and people experience the sights, sounds and smells of the old town. The Meredith family lived in a small community. As the economy was in decline, some people in the town had lost their jobs. Many of their families were struggling to make ends meet. People were trying to help each other meet the challenges.

Mrs. Meredith was a most kind and thoughtful woman. She spent a great deal of time visiting the poor. She knew they had problems, and they needed all kinds of help. When she had time, she would bring food and medicine to them.

One morning she told her children about a family she had visited the day before. There was a man sick in bed, his wife, who took care of him and could not go out to work, and their little boy. The little boy – his name was Bernard – had interested her very much.
“I wish you could see him,” she said to her own children, John, Harry, and Clara. “He is such a help to his mother. He wants very much to earn some money, but I don’t see what he can do.”
After their mother left the room, the children sat thinking about Bernard. “I wish we could help him to earn money,” said Clara. “His family is suffering so much.”
“So do I,” said Harry. “We really should do something to assist them.”
For some moments, John said nothing, but, suddenly, he sprang to his feet and cried, “I have a great idea! I have a solution that we can all help accomplish (完成) .”

The other children also jumped up all attention. When John had an idea, it was sure to be a good one. “I tell you what we can do,” said John. “You know that big box of corn Uncle John sent us? Well, we can make popcorn (爆米花) , and put it into paper bags, and Bernard can take it around to the houses and sell it.”

group-2020-i-reading-a.overview: 这是一则应用文（征诗比赛广告），主题为纪念飞行员 Amelia Earhart 的 POETRY CHALLENGE 征诗活动，介绍写作主题、奖项设置与参赛规则。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文按广告体结构展开：先点明征诗主题，再分层列出三类奖项（Grand Prizes / First Prizes / Honorable Mentions），最后给出参赛规则（字数、书写方式、个人信息、截稿日期）。

paragraphs.summary: 说明征诗主题：写一首关于勇气、决心和力量如何帮助你面对人生挑战的诗，并引出奖项部分。
paragraphs.function: 正文引入，交代写作主题与下文奖项小标题。

paragraphs.summary: 三项大奖：华盛顿之行，每位获奖者可携一名家长和另一人同行，含往返机票、两晚住宿及博物馆与杂志社参观。
paragraphs.function: 奖项细则之一，介绍最高奖内容。

paragraphs.summary: 六项一等奖：一本由作者和飞行员签名的关于 Amelia Earhart 的传记图书。
paragraphs.function: 奖项细则之二，介绍一等奖内容。

paragraphs.summary: 五十项优秀奖：每位获得者将得到一件纪念 Earhart 最后一次飞行的 T 恤，并引出规则部分。
paragraphs.function: 奖项细则之三，介绍优秀奖内容并过渡到规则。

paragraphs.summary: 总则：认真遵守所有规则以免被取消资格。
规则一：诗歌不超过100词，格式与行数不限。
规则二：手写或打印在单张纸上，可用正反两面。
paragraphs.function: 规则细则——书写方式与用纸。

group-2020-i-reading-b.overview: 本文是一篇人物记叙文，讲述了 Jennifer Mauer 凭借超出常人的毅力，克服家庭与经济困难，成为大家庭中第一个获得学士学位（护理专业）的人，并以此激励家人。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文为单段叙事：先点明 Jennifer 需要超常毅力去追求护理学位并最终毕业；再回溯她的成长背景、高中后自费上学并资助弟妹；接着说明她为何重返大学及选择就近项目的原因；随后描写家人的支持以及她为学业所作的牺牲；最后点出她作为第一代毕业生对家庭的激励意义。

paragraphs.summary: 记述 Jennifer Mauer 的求学历程：成长于有 10 个孩子的农场家庭，高中后自费就读技术学院并资助弟妹，婚后为发展事业重返大学，选择就近项目以便兼顾孩子，在家人支持下牺牲陪伴时间，最终以优异成绩毕业，成为家中第一代大学生。
paragraphs.function: 以单段叙事完整呈现人物的奋斗背景、动机、付出与结果，并在结尾升华主题——努力终有回报、激励家人。

group-2020-i-reading-c.overview: 本文是一篇书评，介绍 Toni Bissell 的著作《Chasing the Sea》。文章从作者重返乌兹别克斯坦的缘由谈起，叙述其旅程中遇到的人与事，展现乌兹别克斯坦社会的温暖与阴暗面，并评价该书的写作特点。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文按"背景缘起—成书与人物—旅途见闻—写作评价"四段递进展开：先交代作者重返该国的原因，再引出此书及主要人物，接着列举旅途中的各类经历，最后总评该书风格与价值。

paragraphs.summary: Toni Bissell 上世纪90年代中期在乌兹别克斯坦做志愿者，七个月后身心俱疲离开；几年后因仍被该国吸引而重返，去写一篇关于咸海消失的文章。
paragraphs.function: 交代背景与作者重返乌兹别克斯坦的缘由

paragraphs.summary: 此次造访远超最初目的，由此诞生了《Chasing the Sea》一书，讲述从塔什干到卡拉卡尔帕克斯坦的公路旅行，以及沿途遇到的翻译 Rustam、东道主 Oleg 与 Natasha 等人物。
paragraphs.function: 引出成书缘由、旅程路线与主要人物

paragraphs.summary: 本书是对乌兹别克斯坦生活的速写，既有友善温暖，也有社会阴暗面：在撒马尔罕赞叹建筑奇观，在去布哈拉途中被怀疑贩毒尝到警察手段，在费尔干纳参加葬礼后又遇怪异酒局，在卡拉卡尔帕克斯坦为沙尘暴、疾病和搁浅的渔船而伤感。
paragraphs.function: 列举旅途中丰富多样的见闻与经历

paragraphs.summary: Bissell 巧妙整合历史与文化素材，从西方视角描绘了一幅完整的乌兹别克斯坦图景；其判断与参照颇具美国色彩，全书既非游记也非史书或报道，但生动描绘了最纯粹的中亚传统。
paragraphs.function: 总评该书的写作风格、视角与价值

group-2020-i-reading-d.overview: 本文介绍《消费者研究杂志》的一项研究：用餐同伴的体型与进食量都会影响我们自己的进食量；研究通过两个实验发现，人们会模仿同伴多吃，而当同伴身材瘦却吃得多时，受试者吃得明显更多。

discourseStructure.summary: 首段提出研究结论并引出反直觉观点（真正要避开的是食量大的瘦子），随后描述第一个实验的设计；第二、三段分别给出两个实验的结果；末段解释其背后的社会环境影响机制以及人们如何根据对他人的看法来调整这种影响。

paragraphs.summary: 引用《消费者研究杂志》的研究，指出同伴的体型与进食习惯都会影响我们的进食量，并提出反直觉观点：真正要避开的是食量大的瘦子；随后介绍第一个实验：邀请95名女大学生，以看电影研究为表面理由，由研究者雇佣的演员（自然体重105磅，半数情况下穿增重至180磅的肥胖服）先取食物。
paragraphs.function: 提出研究主题与核心结论，并铺设第一个实验的背景与设计

paragraphs.summary: 第一个实验结果：胖瘦两个版本的演员都取了大量食物，受试者随之取得比平时更多的食物，但在演员偏瘦时受试者取得明显更多。
paragraphs.function: 呈现第一个实验的结果

paragraphs.summary: 第二个实验：瘦演员在一种情况下取2颗糖、另一种情况下取30颗糖，结果与第一个实验相似——受试者跟随，但在瘦演员取30颗时取得明显更多。
paragraphs.function: 呈现第二个实验的结果，进一步佐证结论

paragraphs.summary: 解释社会环境在我们做决定时影响极大（“我也要她点的那种”效应），但我们会调整这种影响：看到胖子大吃会因看到其后果而收敛，而看到瘦子大吃却仍能保持苗条则会跟随。
paragraphs.function: 解释实验背后的社会影响机制及调整影响的依据

trap.explanation: 原文列举的多为建筑赞叹、被疑贩毒、葬礼酒局、沙尘灾害等经历，未提及任何浪漫元素，属无中生有。

evidence.quote: In Samarkand, Mr Bissell admires the architectural wonders, while on his way to Bukhara he gets a taste of police methods when suspected of drug dealing.
evidence.anchor: 建筑奇观、被疑贩毒等接连发生的事件

evidence.quote: In Ferghana, he attends a mountain funeral (葬礼) followed by a strange drinking party.
evidence.anchor: 葬礼后又遇怪异酒局

trap.sourceQuote: This is a quick look at life in Uzbekistan, made of friendliness and warmth, but also its darker side of society.
trap.sourceHighlight: but also its darker side of society
trap.explanation: 原文用 but also its darker side of society 表明旅途既有温暖也有阴暗面，仅取"愉快"以偏概全，缩小了整体经历的范围。

trap.sourceQuote: he gets a taste of police methods when suspected of drug dealing
trap.explanation: 原文仅有被疑贩毒等个别插曲，把全程概括为"危险的"以个别夸大整体，言过其实。

locationParaphrases.targetText: In Ferghana, he attends a mountain funeral (葬礼) followed by a strange drinking party.
locationParaphrases.note: 第三段连续列举撒马尔罕、布哈拉、费尔干纳、卡拉卡尔帕克斯坦各地接连发生的事件，正是 Eventful（多事、经历丰富）的具体体现。

q-2020-i-031.questionFocus: 考查全文写作目的，需结合通篇围绕一本书展开的评述进行判断。
q-2020-i-031.stemTranslationZh: 这篇文章的写作目的是什么？

evidence.quote: Hence this book, Chasing the Sea: Lost Among the Ghosts of Empire in Central Asia
evidence.anchor: 全文围绕 this book 展开

evidence.quote: Whatever it is, the result is a fine and vivid description of the purest of Central Asian traditions.
evidence.anchor: 对该书价值的总评

trap.sourceQuote: Mr Bissell skillfully organizes historical insights and cultural references, making his tale a well-rounded picture of Uzbekistan, seen from Western eyes.
trap.explanation: 原文提到书中含文化参照，但全文目的是介绍该书，并非解释某种文化现象，把局部内容夸大为全文目的。
原文是对在世作者著作的书评，未含任何缅怀纪念之意，属无中生有。

trap.sourceQuote: As the author explains, this is neither a travel nor a history book, or even a piece of reportage.
trap.sourceHighlight: neither a travel nor a history book
trap.explanation: 原文明确该书既非游记也非史书，文章意在介绍此书而非推荐旅游目的地，将书评目的过度泛化为旅游推荐。

locationParaphrases.targetText: Hence this book, Chasing the Sea: Lost Among the Ghosts of Empire in Central Asia
locationParaphrases.note: 全文由 Hence this book 引出并通篇评述该书，写作目的即 To introduce a book（介绍一本书）。

q-2020-i-032.questionFocus: 考查对该研究主旨的把握：这项研究主要讲的是什么。
q-2020-i-032.stemTranslationZh: 这项最新研究主要是关于什么的？

trap.explanation: 原文未提及食品安全（food safety），研究讨论的是进食量与社会影响，与安全无关。

trap.sourceQuote: each woman was asked to help herself to a snack
trap.explanation: 原文中“看电影研究（a study about movie viewership）”只是引导受试者入实验室的表面理由（ostensibly），并非研究真正的主题，以局部细节冒充主旨。

trapEvidence.quote: ostensibly (表面上) participate in a study about movie viewership
trapEvidence.anchor: ostensibly... movie viewership 是表面理由

trap.relationNote: 选项借用原文期刊名中的 Consumer 一词制造干扰，但原文谈的是进食量受社会影响，并未讨论“消费者需求（consumer demand）”。

evidence.quote: both the size and consumption habits of our eating companions can influence our food intake
evidence.anchor: 同伴影响我们的进食量

evidence.quote: To test the effect of social influence on eating habits
evidence.anchor: 研究社会影响对进食习惯的作用

locationParaphrases.targetText: the effect of social influence on eating habits
locationParaphrases.note: 选项 Eating behavior 与原文 eating habits / food intake 同义，研究主题即进食行为受社会影响。

q-2020-i-033.questionFocus: 考查对划线词 beanpoles 的词义推测，需结合上下文判断其指代对象。
q-2020-i-033.stemTranslationZh: 第一段中划线词 “beanpoles” 指的是什么？

trap.sourceQuote: it’s the beanpoles with big appetites you really need to avoid
trap.explanation: 原文中 beanpoles 后接 with big appetites，“食量大”是 beanpoles 的附加修饰，而非 beanpoles 一词本身的含义；beanpoles 指的是身材，错把修饰语当作词义。

trapEvidence.quote: it’s the beanpoles with big appetites you really need to avoid
trapEvidence.anchor: big appetites 是附加修饰，非词义本身

trap.sourceQuote: contrary to existing research that says you should avoid eating with heavier people who order large portions (份) , it’s the beanpoles with big appetites you really need to avoid
trap.sourceHighlight: contrary to existing research that says you should avoid eating with heavier people
trap.explanation: 原文用 contrary to 将 beanpoles 与 heavier people（超重的人）对立起来，beanpoles 恰恰与超重相反，指偏瘦的人，选项把含义颠倒。

trapEvidence.quote: contrary to existing research that says you should avoid eating with heavier people who order large portions
trapEvidence.anchor: contrary to heavier people，与超重相反

trap.explanation: 原文未提及挑食（picky eaters），beanpoles 描述的是身材瘦高，与是否挑食无关。

evidence.quote: contrary to existing research that says you should avoid eating with heavier people who order large portions (份) , it’s the beanpoles with big appetites you really need to avoid
evidence.anchor: 与 heavier people 形成对比，故为瘦人

evidence.quote: But if a thin person eats a lot, I’ll follow suit. If he can eat much and keep slim, why can’t I?
evidence.anchor: 下文将其等同于 thin / slim 的人

locationParaphrases.targetText: But if a thin person eats a lot, I’ll follow suit. If he can eat much and keep slim, why can’t I?
locationParaphrases.note: beanpoles 与原文 thin person / keep slim 同义，beanpole 本义为“豆架/竹竿”，引申指身材瘦高的人。

locationParaphrases.targetText: contrary to existing research that says you should avoid eating with heavier people who order large portions (份) , it’s the beanpoles with big appetites you really need to avoid
locationParaphrases.note: 通过 contrary to ... heavier people 的对比定位，可推断 beanpoles 与 heavier people 相反，即偏瘦的人。

q-2020-i-034.questionFocus: 考查对实验设计意图的理解：研究者为何雇佣演员。
q-2020-i-034.stemTranslationZh: 研究者为什么要雇佣这名演员？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 为了观察她会如何影响受试者。

evidence.quote: To test the effect of social influence on eating habits, the researchers conducted two experiments.
evidence.anchor: 为测社会影响而做实验

evidence.quote: An actor hired by the researchers grabbed her food first.
evidence.anchor: 演员先取食物以施加影响

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 为了测试受试者是否能认出她。

trap.claim: 雇佣演员是为了测试受试者能否认出她。
trap.explanation: 原文未提及让受试者“认出”演员（recognize her），雇佣演员的目的是施加社会影响，而非辨认。

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 为了弄清楚她在两个实验中会做什么。

trap.optionText: To find out what she would do in the two tests．
trap.explanation: 演员的行为是研究者预先设计安排的（取大量食物/取30颗糖），并非要“发现”演员会做什么；研究真正观察的是受试者（participants）的反应，对象错配。

trapEvidence.quote: The participants followed suit, taking more food than they normally would have.

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 为了研究她为什么能控制住自己的体重。

trap.claim: 雇佣演员是为了研究她为何能保持体重不增。
trap.explanation: 原文未提及研究演员“为何能保持体重”，演员体重由肥胖服人为控制，目的在于影响受试者，而非研究演员本人减重。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: To see how she would affect the participants．
locationParaphrases.targetText: To test the effect of social influence on eating habits, the researchers conducted two experiments.
locationParaphrases.note: 选项 how she would affect the participants 与原文 the effect of social influence on eating habits 同义，演员即社会影响的载体。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: Why did the researchers hire the actor
locationParaphrases.targetText: An actor hired by the researchers grabbed her food first.
locationParaphrases.note: 题干 hire the actor 对应原文 An actor hired by the researchers，由其 grabbed her food first 可定位雇佣演员是为施加影响。

q-2020-i-035.questionFocus: 考查末段细节推断：我们依据什么来“调整这种影响”。
q-2020-i-035.stemTranslationZh: 根据最后一段，我们依据什么来“调整这种影响”？

trap.claim: 我们依据自己有多饿来调整影响。
trap.explanation: 原文未提及饥饿程度（how hungry we are），调整依据是对他人的看法，而非自身饥饿。

trap.sourceText: If he can eat much and keep slim
trap.optionText: How slim we want to be．
trap.relationNote: 选项借用原文中描述他人的 slim 一词，但原文 keep slim 指的是“那个瘦人”能保持苗条，调整依据是我们如何看待他人，而非我们自己想多苗条。

trapEvidence.quote: If he can eat much and keep slim, why can’t I?

evidence.quote: If an overweight person is having a large portion, I’ll hold back a bit because I see the results of his eating habits.
evidence.anchor: 因看到胖子的后果而收敛

evidence.quote: But if a thin person eats a lot, I’ll follow suit. If he can eat much and keep slim, why can’t I?
evidence.anchor: 因瘦人能保持苗条而跟随

trap.claim: 我们依据自己对食物的感受来调整影响。
trap.explanation: 原文未提及对食物本身的感受（how we feel about the food），调整依据是对同伴（胖/瘦及其结果）的看法。

locationParaphrases.targetText: If an overweight person is having a large portion, I’ll hold back a bit because I see the results of his eating habits.
locationParaphrases.note: 选项 perceive others 与原文据他人胖瘦（overweight person / thin person）及其后果来决定跟随与否对应，即依据对他人的看法来调整影响。

locationParaphrases.targetText: However, we’ll adjust the influence.
locationParaphrases.note: 题干 adjust the influence 直接对应原文 we’ll adjust the influence，其后 If ... overweight ... / But if a thin person ... 给出调整依据。
